"Oh. I'm sorry." Angela sat back. "My name is Angela. I came here with the army. I sent the Legions and the Enders in. I'm so very sorry."
Layla stared. This was the enemy from the screen. "Stop saying sorry!"
Angela gave a tiny, wobbling smile. "You're very loud. I think it's rather nice. I'd like to be your friend, if you'd let me."
She held out her hand, stiffly, and pulled Angela up. "...You're not so bad," she muttered. She marched off.
"Inconclusive," said Layla, and ran round the corner.

Pip mended the drains and the old pump in the square. When clear water ran at last, he whispered, "I wish Corvin could see it. And Daisy." Angela knelt and hugged him, and he whistled softly. It was, as far as anyone could tell, a song.
Angela had put Tetra in Ruby's hands to mend. Ruby was afraid to try. On the thirty-first night, Chang'e let her into the lab, and they worked until four in the morning.

"I lost my parents when the Base fell," said Chang'e quietly. "I hated the person who wasn't there. What helped was being held by the person I'd blamed." She looked at Tetra. "He made a choice. It wasn't yours to take back. You say thank you, and you carry it."
At dawn Tetra woke and chirped. Ruby carried him to the garden, where Angela sat alone on a bench. Tetra lifted his head and trilled.
"Oh," said Angela. It was all she said.

"No," said Lesley. "Nobody does. A badge is not a payment. It is given so that you know somebody saw."
She pinned the star on the grey coat. Ruby's tears fell on the floor. "I'll try to deserve it."

They walked up the aisle with half a pace between them. Guinevere had her chin up. Vexana looked at the floor. Each wore a gold star at her collar.
Lesley looked at them for a long time. Then something at the corner of her mouth changed. It was a smile. Almost nobody in the hall had ever seen it.

"I'm proud of you," said Lesley. "Both of you. I have seen many good fighters. I have never seen two fight like that. It was like watching one person with four hands. When it is very dark, remember this day."

Guinevere held the star up in the sun. "We're the best partners in the Aspirants!" she cried. She was crying. So was Vexana. Vexana took her hand and raised it, in front of everyone.
At the back, Ruby bent her head and smiled. It was the first time in a long while that anyone had looked so happy.
It would not last. But nobody in that bright hall could have known.

"Teacher Chang'e told us how to defeat the Will of the Planet," said Guinevere. "We must destroy the Ender's Control Core, hidden in its dark void."
"She said we can't get near it," said Vexana. "She said it was impossible."

"Don't worry. I will definitely find a way." Her eyes blazed. "I don't care if it's at the bottom of the sea. I'll fly there with my bare hands. I'll do it for everyone. For the whole world. But mostly," she said, going pink, "for you."
Vexana did not answer. She looked pale. She was thinking very hard.

It was a dark idea. It came into her mind like a stranger into a lit room, and stood in the corner with its hands folded.
It has nothing to do with me.
Guinevere lay down again with her eyes shut. "That's settled. I'll find a way. And you will read all the books and write a paper. You're so clever. You'll find out how."
"That's all anyone can do," said Guinevere, drowsily.
She did not see Vexana's hand stop on her hair. She did not see it tremble. She did not see the violet eyes fill with light.
"Yes," said Vexana, very low. "That's all anyone can do."
She went on stroking the peach-gold hair while the leaves came down. The girl in her lap fell asleep. Vexana looked up at the sky. It was a high, clear, tender blue.
She did not know that she would not see a sky like it again for a long time.
